cek0: Mallet Finger: How Long to Wear a Splint, Care and Exercises | İhsan Eren
cek1: Has your fingertip dropped and won’t straighten? What mallet finger is, how long to wear a splint, how to clean it and when surgery is needed. Four exercises for during and after splinting.
cek3: Did a ball hit your fingertip, or did you stub your finger hard, and now the tip droops and you cannot straighten it on your own? The tendon that straightens the end joint may have torn, or come away from where it attaches together with a small piece of bone. Treatment is usually simple but needs patience: the fingertip is kept straight in a splint for weeks, without ever bending.

cek14: Why the splint matters so much
cek15: By keeping the end joint straight, the splint lets the torn tendon or piece of bone heal in place.
cek16: Wear the splint day and night without taking it off, including in the bath or shower and in bed.
cek17: The splint should fit firmly, your fingertip should reach the end of it, and it should not stop the middle joint bending.
cek18: Smoking and diabetes can slow healing.
cek19: Clean the splint once a day
cek20: Skin that stays wet under the splint gets sore very quickly. Keep your finger and the splint dry, and do not cover the splint’s ventilation holes with tape. Someone can help you with these steps.
cek21: Rest your finger flat on a table with the end joint straight.
cek22: Cut the tape and slide the splint off; keep your fingertip flat on the table.
cek23: Wash your finger and the splint with soapy water and dry them, without bending your fingertip at any point.
cek24: Slide the splint back on while your fingertip is straight and fix it with non-stretch tape; the tape should go around the middle of the splint and not cover the middle joint.
cek25: Four exercises for during and after splinting
cek26: Do the first exercise while wearing the splint. Start the other three when the continuous splinting period (6 or 8 weeks) has ended and your team agrees; during this time, keep wearing the splint for another 2–4 weeks at night and for heavy or risky tasks. If your fingertip starts to droop again while exercising, stop, wear the splint all the time and contact your team.
cek27: Bending the middle joint in the splint
cek28: Bending the middle joint while wearing the splint
cek29: Without removing the splint, fully bend and straighten the middle joint of your injured finger; the end joint stays straight inside the splint. Move your other fingers fully too, so they do not get stiff.
cek32: Start after the continuous splinting period has ended. Straighten your fingers and thumb as far as you can and spread them apart.
cek33: Hold for 10–20 seconds, little and often
cek35: Keeping the knuckles at the base of your fingers straight, bend only the middle and end joints, then straighten your fingers. Stop if the end joint starts to droop.
cek37: Slowly make a full fist, then open your fingers completely. Your finger may feel stiff at first; work little and often without forcing it.
cek38: Usually not; most mallet fingers do well with a splint alone. Surgery may be needed if a large piece of bone has come away with the tendon. It is usually a day-case procedure under local anaesthetic, fixed with fine wires that stay in for 3–4 weeks.
cek39: What happens if my fingertip bends while I’m wearing the splint?
cek40: During the continuous splinting period, even a single bend of the end joint can damage the healing tendon and delay healing; the splinting period often starts again from the beginning. Only take the splint off for cleaning, with your finger resting flat on a table. If this has happened, tell your team.
cek42: It recovers well for most people, but even with the best treatment a lag of up to 10 degrees at the end joint is common. Swelling, tenderness and redness over the back of the finger can take a few months to settle. When a piece of bone came away, a small bump may remain over the joint; this usually does not affect how the hand works.
cek43: When can I drive and return to sport?
cek44: You can drive when you can grip the steering wheel firmly without pain distracting you; check with your insurer about driving with a splint. One NHS leaflet advises avoiding sport for at least 8 weeks; decide when to return with your team.
cek45: Why shouldn’t I wear a ring?
cek46: The finger may swell, and a ring can affect blood flow and healing. Do not wear a ring on the injured finger while you are in the splint.
